properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-28 (v0.74.0): the --remote client forwards every call unchanged apart from the bearer header and a handshake notice, and never sends _meta["reflow2/writes_for"]. Point 2 of the requirement asks for that on every call, and no planned step names it: position 7 names only point 3
properties.statement:
OBSERVED while mapping the code for combined-plan position 7 (epoch:planned-local-files-are-measured-for-a-remote-design).
· crates/reflow2-mcp/src/proxy.rs: Remote::send posts the raw stdin line unchanged (proxy.rs 312-358).
· mcp_http.rs adds only the Authorization: Bearer header (289-291).
· with_notice prepends a notice to the handshake's instructions (proxy.rs 434).
· grep finds "writes_for" in none of proxy.rs, mcp_http.rs, main.rs or pointer.rs. Only the server reads the key (service.rs:638, WRITES_FOR_META).

req:a-local-client-works-against-a-remote-reflow2-server-by-url, point 2: "On a stateless server the only way to say it is per request, so the client carries `_meta[\"reflow2/writes_for\"]` on every call it forwards ... A shared credential says which client, never which person."

WHY IT HAS NOT BITTEN YET, as far as is known: on flo2.io each person signs in with their own credential, and the gateway binds the writer from it (flo2's fact:root-cause-the-door-rebinds-approver-and-says-so-only-in-its-refusal-2026-09-28). The gap shows on an organisation's shared server reached with ONE shared key, the case point 2 was written for. There, every write would be credited to whoever the key names, or to nobody.

WHERE IT STANDS IN THE PLAN: the requirement is SCHEDULED_FOR position 7's epoch as a whole, but the epoch's text says it "delivers point 3". No other planned step names point 2.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any shared-key server exists yet (none is known); whether the client would learn the person's contributor id from setup, from the server's credential check, or from a flag.

ALSO UNBUILT, found the same day while reviewing GitHub issue #616: point 1's "A SIGN-IN FLOW (browser or device code) for a server that offers one". client_setup.rs says "Browser sign-in is a later step; the shape leaves room for it as another `KeySource`." No planned step in the combined plan names it either. Issue #616 measures its cost: a team behind an OIDC identity provider pastes a Bearer token into `.mcp.json` per person and re-pastes it when it expires, because neither their MCP client (the server does not say it is a protected resource) nor reflow2's --remote client runs the flow. So of the requirement's three points, only point 3 is scheduled (position 7), and points 1 and 2 are in no step.
